indicators.title: Electoral democracy
indicators.source: V-Dem, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: How far elections are free and fair, with free expression and association. 1 is the most democratic.

indicators.title: Human rights
indicators.source: V-Dem, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: Freedom from political killing and torture, and freedom of movement, religion and expression. 1 is the most respected.

indicators.title: Press freedom
indicators.source: Reporters Without Borders, World Press Freedom Index
indicators.note: Reporters Without Borders' World Press Freedom Index score. Higher means a freer press.

indicators.title: Clean government
indicators.source: Transparency International, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: Transparency International's Corruption Perceptions Index. Higher means less perceived public-sector corruption.

indicators.title: GDP per person
indicators.source: World Bank, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: Economic output per person, adjusted for what money buys locally (purchasing power parity).

indicators.title: Median income
indicators.unit: dollars a day, adjusted for prices
indicators.source: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: What the person in the exact middle lives on each day, from household surveys, adjusted for local prices.

indicators.title: Living on under $3 a day
indicators.source: World Bank Poverty and Inequality Platform, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: The share of people below the World Bank's international poverty line of $3 a day (2021 prices).

indicators.title: Inequality
indicators.source: World Bank, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: How unequally income or consumption is shared. 0 is perfect equality, 1 is one person holding everything.

indicators.title: Government debt
indicators.note: General government gross debt as a share of the economy. IMF figures for the latest year are estimates.

indicators.title: Military spending
indicators.source: SIPRI, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: Military spending as a share of the economy, from the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute.

indicators.title: Murder rate
indicators.source: UN Office on Drugs and Crime, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: Intentional homicides per 100,000 people a year.

indicators.title: Median age
indicators.source: UN World Population Prospects, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: Half the population is younger than this, half older.

indicators.title: Children per woman
indicators.source: UN World Population Prospects, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: The average number of children a woman would have at current rates. About 2.1 keeps a population stable.

indicators.title: Life expectancy
indicators.source: UN World Population Prospects, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: How long a newborn would live on average at current death rates.

indicators.title: Life satisfaction
indicators.source: World Happiness Report, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: People rate their lives from 0 (worst possible) to 10 (best possible), averaged over three years.

indicators.title: Online
indicators.source: ITU, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: The share of people who used the internet in the past three months.

indicators.title: Living in cities
indicators.source: UN World Urbanization Prospects, via Our World in Data
indicators.note: The share of people living in urban areas, by each country's own definition.
